problems: E27 changes the EHF binding account: EHF occupancy at the variant has been observed in RWPE-1, although not in cranial neural crest and not in an allele-specific assay. H3's binding claim should no longer say that EHF binding at the site has not been demonstrated.

The QBiC-SELEX results, including the TFAP2C own-model result in E26 and EHF-mapped models in E25, predict allele-dependent binding in vitro; they do not establish occupancy or allelic imbalance in the disease-relevant cell type.

IRF6 is a plausible but not uniquely resolved target. The cleft credible-set support is modest, while E06 also links the element to UTP25 and reports UTP25 eQTLs for the exact variant in several non-craniofacial tissues.

The cleft association is for orofacial clefts, not specifically cleft lip, and does not connect any predicted binding change to a direction of IRF6 expression or disease risk. The reported GWAS effect allele A is not enough to infer the direction of the proposed regulatory mechanism.

games.reason: Both chains share the same element, IRF6, cell-type, and phenotype evidence, so those links do not distinguish them. A is better supported at the TF-binding link: TFAP2C has its own QBiC-SELEX model predicting stronger binding for G than A (E26). B’s ref-favoring prediction comes from a ZNF76 model, not a stated ZNF143 model (E14). Neither chain has ChIP-seq demonstrating occupancy at the variant; the reported peaks are elsewhere, and expression context is unknown (E13, E14).

The shared element, IRF6, cell-type, and phenotype evidence does not distinguish the chains. B has the more direct TF-specific allelic-binding support: TFAP2C has an own QBiC-SELEX model predicting stronger binding for G than A (E26), consistent with the AP-2 family prediction (E13). A’s ref-favoring prediction comes from a ZNF76 model assigned within the ZF family, while ZNF143 is the named candidate member (E14); neither chain has demonstrated occupancy at the variant or relevant-cell expression. Thus B is better supported comparatively, but its full mechanism remains unestablished.
